restated_task: Refactor kvparse.parser.parse_line to use str.partition instead of manual index loops, stripping key and value, raising ValueError for missing '=' or empty key, and removing matching surrounding quotes from values of length >=2; also extract the ignorable-line detection into a private module-level function _is_ignorable that returns True for lines that are empty or start with '#' or ';' after stripping, and update parse to use it. The observable behavior of parse and parse_line must remain identical for all string inputs, including exception types and duplicate-key handling; parse must still raise TypeError for non-string input. The existing test suite must pass unchanged.

interface_contract.name: parse_line
interface_contract.behavior: Split the input line at the first '=' using str.partition. Strip whitespace from the key part and the value part. If no '=' is found, raise ValueError. If the stripped key is empty, raise ValueError. If the stripped value has length >= 2 and its first and last characters are both double quotes (") or both single quotes ('), remove those surrounding quotes. Return the (key, value) tuple.
error_cases: ValueError if stripped key is empty

interface_contract.name: parse
interface_contract.behavior: If text is not a string, raise TypeError. Split text into lines with splitlines(). For each raw line, if _is_ignorable(raw) returns True, skip it. Otherwise, call parse_line(raw) to obtain a (key, value) pair and insert into the result dictionary, with later occurrences of the same key overwriting earlier ones. Return the result dictionary.
error_cases: TypeError if text is not a str
ValueError if any non-ignorable line causes parse_line to raise ValueError

interface_contract.name: _is_ignorable
interface_contract.behavior: Strip the input line. Return True if the stripped line is empty or its first character is '#' or ';'. Otherwise return False.

acceptance_criteria: parse_line('k e y = v') returns ('k e y','v').
parse_line contains no 'while' loop and uses str.partition.

parse handles comments: parse('# comment

; other
name = x
') returns {'name': 'x'}.
parse handles blank lines and Windows line endings (e.g., '\r\n') as before.
parse later duplicate keys win: parse('a=1\na=2') returns {'a': '2'}.
parse raises ValueError for a malformed line anywhere in the text (e.g., parse('novalue\n') raises ValueError).
parse raises TypeError for non-string input (None, 3, a list, bytes).
_is_ignorable exists in kvparse.parser and returns True for '   # c', '', '\t; c'.
_is_ignorable returns False for 'a = 1' and 'a = # not a comment'.
The existing tests in tests/ pass unchanged.
out_of_scope: Must not modify the test files.
Must not change the public exports (parse, parse_line) from kvparse.
Must not change the behavior of parse_line for non-string arguments (unspecified).
Must not change exception messages (they are not prescribed).
Must not add new public functions or classes.
Must not change the handling of duplicate keys (later wins).
Must not change the quote removal logic (only matching surrounding quotes on stripped value of length >=2).
